newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Kia creditors again delay bailout decision.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Kia creditors again delay bailout decision.

text.p: Creditors of South Korea's Kia Group on Friday delayed for the second time a decision on bailing out the troubled carmaker, an official from one of the creditor banks said.
Creditors would meet on August 4 at 0600 GMT, he said.
No decision was reached during Friday's meeting because of continuing disagreement between creditors and Kia management about two core issues, the bank official said.
Creditors have demanded that Kia executives, including group chairman Kim Sun-hong, resign and that the group sell off its commercial vehicle maker, Asia Motors Corp.
Kia, South Korea's eighth-largest conglomerate, has said its management would resign if the group's self-rescue measures failed.
The group also has said Asia Motors would sell off part of its assets before it was absorbed by Kia Motors to serve as an assembly plant.
Speaking to reporters later at a news conference, Kwon Woo-ha, a senior executive at Korea First Bank, said creditors were disappointed with Kia.
"Our demand has not been met at all. We still want the Kia management to resign unconditionally," Kwon said.
He said creditors also demanded in Friday's meeting that Kia secure its unions' confirmation on worker curtailments.

But Kwon said creditors had not made a final decision on the sale of Asia Motors. Kia told creditors it had hired several consulting firms to study the advantages and disadvantages of selling off Asia Motors or merging it, he said.
